Assuming a reliability of 80% and no other modifiers, the average amount of aircraft lost per hour would be 0.014% of a wing per airbase. This accumulates to 0.336% of a wing per airbase per day and 122.64% of an air wing per airbase per year.

All aircraft (other than ⟦0⟧ with ⟦1⟧) start with a reliability of at least 80%, though this can be modified up or down through the use of ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧. With a reliability of 90% and no other modifiers, the average hourly loss rate from accidents would become 0.007% of a wing per airbase, which translates to 0.168% of a wing per airbase per day and 61.32% of an air wing per airbase per year. With a reliability of 40% (common with ⟦4⟧ without ⟦5⟧'s ⟦6⟧) and no other modifiers, the average hourly loss rate from accidents would become 0.042% of a wing per airbase, which translates to 1.008% of a wing per airbase per day and 367.92% of an air wing per airbase per year.
Due to how low the losses from accidents are when compared to actual combat, it's usually preferable to disregard reliability in favor of combat stats in most situations.
